claims.text: The platform's own recorded distances establish the deviation: the trip ran 9.4 km against a recommended route of 8.2 km, a deviation of 1.20 km, which is above the 1.0 km tolerance, so the deviation is established on the recorded distances and is not within tolerance.

The GPS trace corroborates which route was taken and when: after fixes on the Pan-Island Expressway the vehicle is on Bedok North Road from 09:26:25 and on Upper Changi Road from 09:30:25, and only rejoins Still Road at 09:33:55. The trace is used to show the route taken, not to re-measure the distance, so it does not disturb the recorded 9.4 km figure.

The reroute was not traffic-justified. The only traffic data for the recommended PIE segment (Bedok North Road to Still Road, towards Tuas), overlapping the trip window, records type NONE with no incident, roadwork or closure and speed bands 4-6; POL-RD-23 requires congestion, an incident or a closure intersecting the recommended route, and it expressly provides that a driver's assertion of traffic with no such data does not justify the reroute. The driver's statement that the PIE stretch 'always crawl' is exactly such an unevidenced assertion.

The driver did not inform the rider of the deviation as POL-RD-21 requires. The chat log holds only two entries, at 09:17:50 and 09:18:15, both about the pickup meeting point and both before the trip started at 09:19:25; the trip record's messages_during_trip is empty and the record carries no in-app calls at all. The deviation began at 09:26:44, so no notice was given before or at the point of deviation, and any unrecorded verbal notice cannot be established under POL-GEN-26.

On those facts row (d) of the refund matrix applies - not traffic-justified, deviation over 1 km - and the excess distance fare is refunded in full. That fare is the deviation distance times the per-km rate: 1.20 km x 0.92 SGD = 1.10 SGD, rounded to the cent, without surge. The rider should therefore not carry that part of the charge.

I do not overreach on quantum: the rider asked for 4.00 SGD, but the policy's measure of the disputed distance is the excess distance fare, and on this record that measure is 1.10 SGD and no more. The rider's case is put at that figure, which is the whole of what the matrix provides.

The chat log holds only two entries, at 09:17:50 and 09:18:15, both about the pickup meeting point and both before the trip started at 09:19:25; the trip record's messages_during_trip is empty and the record carries no in-app calls at all. The deviation began at 09:26:44, so no notice was given before or at the point of deviation, and any unrecorded verbal notice cannot be established under POL-GEN-26.

On those facts row (d) of the refund matrix applies - not traffic-justified, deviation over 1 km - and the excess distance fare is refunded in full. That fare is the deviation distance times the per-km rate: 1.20 km x 0.92 SGD = 1.10 SGD, rounded to the cent, without surge. The rider should therefore not carry that part of the charge.

I do not overreach on quantum: the rider asked for 4.00 SGD, but the policy's measure of the disputed distance is the excess distance fare, and on this record that measure is 1.10 SGD and no more. The rider's case is put at that figure, which is the whole of what the matrix provides.

The rider's recovery is capped by POL-RD-24 at the excess distance fare and nothing more: 1.20 km of deviation at the metered rate of 0.92 SGD/km is 1.10 SGD, without surge and rounded to the cent, and the payments ledger's own money derivation reaches the same 1.10 SGD figure — not the 4.00 SGD the rider asks for.

The 4.00 SGD in the rider's claim is the contested sum, not the remedy: POL-GEN-22 takes the dispute value from dispute.amount_contested_sgd, while POL-RD-24 fixes what is paid, and the itemised metered fare the rider was charged carries no deviation or distance surcharge beyond the 9.4 km actually driven — base fare 3.80, distance fare 8.65, time fare 4.08, platform fee 0.90, with zero surge, zero tolls ERP and no refund already issued.

The deviation on this record is one bounded segment of 1.20 km: the platform's recorded 9.4 km actual against the 8.2 km recommended route under POL-RD-22, and the trace fixes confirm the driver left the recommended route only at the PIE / Bedok North Road exit and rejoined it at Still Road / Upper Changi Road. Nothing in the record supports a longer or repeated deviation, so the exposure cannot be stretched to the whole contested fare.

The driver does not press the no-refund rows of the matrix: his statement that the PIE Bedok stretch 'always crawl[s]' is an assertion with no corroboration in the record, and the LTA advisory covering the recommended segment and the trip window is of type NONE, with its own derivation recording justifies_reroute = false, so POL-RD-23's traffic justification is not established and the no-refund rows are not reached; the case runs on POL-RD-24(d).

A full return of the contested 4.00 SGD is not open on this record: the rider is not entirely right, because the charge he paid is an ordinary metered fare for the route actually driven and the deviation was 1.20 km of a 9.4 km trip, so the outcome is the partial return POL-GEN-03 describes — the 1.10 SGD excess distance fare — and the rest of the metered charge stands.
